citations.narrative:
A large, open bag of puppy food was stored directly on the floor in the food storage room. Open bags of food may cause
nutrient loss, become contaminated and create a potential environment for growth of mold and bacteria. Supplies of food
and bedding must be stored in a manner that protects the supplies from spoilage, contamination, and vermin infestation.
The supplies must be stored off the floor and away from the walls, to allow cleaning underneath and around the supplies.
All open supplies of food and bedding must be kept in leakproof containers with tightly fitting lids to prevent contamination
and spoilage. A system of appropriate protection of food supplies must be in place.
Correct by 10/30/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
